question: A uniformly charged thin spherical shell of radius $R$ has electric field magnitude $E$ at its surface $(r = R)$. At a point $Q$ located at $r = 3R$ from the center, state the field magnitude and give the reason.

options.A: $E/3$ — because the field outside falls as $1/r$.
options.B: $E/9$ — because outside a spherically symmetric charge distribution the field is that of a point charge at the center, so $E \propto 1/r^2$ and $E(3R) = E \times \left(\dfrac{R^2}{(3R)^2}\right)$.
options.C: $E$ — because field lines are radial so the magnitude stays the same along a radius.
options.D: $0$ — because the field of a shell is zero both inside and outside.
